explanation: Aquatic ecosystems are classified into freshwater (inland), saltwater (marine), or brackish water (a mixture of fresh and salt water). Wetlands are ecosystems that remain wet for at least part of the year and are categorized into three main types: 1) Marshes: wetlands that are frequently or continually inundated by water. 2) Swamps: wetlands dominated by woody trees or shrubs. 3) Bogs: wetlands characterized by highly acidic waters, peat deposits, and sphagnum moss.

questions.q: What defines a swamp compared to a marsh or a bog?
opts: Swamps are characterized by acidic waters and peat deposits.
Swamps are dominated by woody plants or shrubs.
Swamps are continually inundated but have no vegetation.
Swamps are composed entirely of brackish water.
